UX / UI Flow Review

Merged review of the merchant dashboard and PopApp customer app — brand/colour consistency, naming clarity, and process confusion · accept / reject + comment inline · 2026-08-27
Severity: HIGH broken / likely to block MED confusing / friction LOW polish NEW added 08-27
15 findings (8 new on 2026-08-27, the rest carried over from the 08-22 pass and still open), self-contained with screenshots embedded. Toggle each Accept / Reject, add a comment, then Save reviewed copy and send the file back.
Checked on prod: eventtestwill.unico-app.com/dashboard (merchant) and eventtestwill.shop.unico-app.com (customer). Button colours were read from the live DOM (computed background-color), not eyeballed. Brand reference: #4F81FF — the dominant colour in the dashboard codebase (46 uses) and the logo. Scope = popapp system behaviour, not the test merchant’s placeholder content.

Merchant dashboard — brand & naming (new)

1 Primary buttons render near-black instead of the Unico blue HIGH NEW

ProblemThe main call-to-action on almost every screen is black. Measured live: “Create New Event” and “Create Coupon” both compute to background rgba(9, 9, 11, 0.9) — near-black — while the Unico brand blue is #4F81FF / rgb(79, 129, 255).
Why it confusesThe product’s most prominent controls don’t look like Unico at all. The brand blue IS used on the same pages for headings, the logo and icon chips, so the page reads as two unrelated design systems — a black “app chrome” and a blue brand.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard — Events → Event Planning (“Create New Event”), Promotions → Coupons (“Create Coupon”), and most other primary CTAs.
Suggested fixAdd a Unico brand entry (#4F81FF) to the shared Button palette and make it the default for primary actions. Root cause: src/components/button.jsx:165 falls back to Catalyst’s `dark/zinc` — `styles.colors[color ?? 'dark/zinc']`. 272 of 306 <Button> usages pass no colour at all, so they all inherit black; the palette ships ~20 Tailwind colours and has no brand colour.

2 Login button is indigo — a third “primary” colour MED NEW

ProblemThe sign-in button computes to rgb(79, 70, 229) = #4F46E5 (Tailwind indigo-600). That is neither the brand blue #4F81FF nor the near-black used elsewhere in the dashboard.
Why it confusesThis is the very first screen a merchant sees, and the logo sits directly above the button in brand blue — so the mismatch is visible side by side. Across the product there are now three different “primary” colours: indigo (login), black (dashboard CTAs), blue (brand/app).
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → sign-in page (/home/login).
Suggested fixUse the brand blue #4F81FF for the Login button so the first impression matches the logo directly above it.

3 Sidebar labels are truncated LOW NEW

ProblemLeft-nav items are cut off mid-word — “Membership …” on Promotions, “Ongoing Eve…” on Events.
Why it confusesThe merchant has to guess or hover to know what a nav item is. It also looks unfinished next to the otherwise-clean layout.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Promotions sidebar (“Membership …”), Events sidebar (“Ongoing Eve…”).
Suggested fixWiden the sidebar, shorten the labels (e.g. “Membership”, “Ongoing”), or wrap to two lines instead of clipping.

4 Payment Dashboard exposes the Finix processor and offers a “Sandbox Account” HIGH NEW

ProblemFinancials → Payment Dashboard renders a bare third-party <b>FINIX</b> logo with a loading spinner, under it: “Don’t have an account? <b>Create a Sandbox Account</b>”.
Why it confusesTwo problems at once. (1) The merchant is dropped into another company’s branding with no explanation — they signed up for Unico and have no idea what “Finix” is or why it wants an account. (2) A <b>sandbox</b> (developer test) account is being offered inside the <b>production</b> dashboard — a real merchant clicking it would create a test account and expect real payouts.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Financials → Payment Dashboard.
Suggested fixWrap the embed in Unico framing that explains what it is (“Your payment processor account”), and never surface the sandbox sign-up link in production — it should be hidden outside dev/test environments.

5 Users list is filled with anonymous visitor records MED NEW

ProblemUsers → User List is dominated by auto-generated accounts (“UC_m_0088”, “UC_m_2625”, …) with no Phone, no Email, Purchase Count 0 and $0 spent. Every anonymous visit appears to create one.
Why it confusesThe merchant opens “Users” expecting customers, and instead sees pages of empty ghost records with machine names. Real buyers are buried, and metrics like “Purchase Count” are meaningless at list level. The Status column is also just an unlabeled toggle — it isn’t clear what it enables/disables, and there is no confirmation.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Users → User List.
Suggested fixDefault the list to users with contact details or at least one order (with a filter/toggle to include anonymous visitors), and label the Status toggle with what it does.

Customer app — brand & naming (new)

6 Event theme colour doesn’t carry into checkout MED NEW

ProblemAn event page is themed per event — event 205 renders teal (Buy Now = linear-gradient from rgb(15,118,110)). But once the buyer continues, the checkout / payment screens switch to blue buttons (“Continue to Card Payment”, “Pay with a new card”).
Why it confusesWithin a single purchase the buyer crosses from a teal-branded event into blue system screens, which reads like leaving the event (or even the site) — exactly at the moment trust matters most, on a payment page.
Where in UICustomer app → Event detail (themed) → checkout → payment-pending → card form (unthemed blue).
Suggested fixCarry the event/store theme colour through the checkout and payment screens, or deliberately use one neutral system colour for the whole purchase flow — but not a different one per step.

7 “More Services” is a vague catch-all LOW NEW

ProblemThe Profile groups Wallet, Tickets, Coupons, Messages, Points, Membership and Settings under a single heading called “More Services”.
Why it confuses“More Services” doesn’t describe any of them — Tickets and Settings are not “services”. It gives no clue where to find a ticket, which is the single most important item for an event buyer.
Where in UICustomer app → Profile → “More Services” section.
Suggested fixSplit into meaningful groups (e.g. “My Tickets & Wallet” vs “Account”), or surface Tickets outside the group since it’s the primary reason a buyer opens the app.

8 The magnifier tab opens “Custom Page 1”, not search MED NEW

ProblemThe middle item in the customer app’s bottom tab bar uses a magnifying-glass (search) icon, but tapping it opens a content page whose title is “Custom Page 1”.
Why it confusesThe icon promises search — the standard meaning of a magnifier — and delivers an unrelated content page. On top of that the page shows “Custom Page 1”, an unconfigured internal default, to real customers. A buyer looking for an event has no way to search.
Where in UICustomer app → bottom tab bar (middle icon) → “Custom Page 1”.
Suggested fixMatch icon to destination: either make it real search, or give the tab an icon and label that describe the custom page. And require a real page title before a custom page can be published.

Customer app — flow (from 08-22)

9 “Buy Now” is active before a package is selected MED

ProblemThe event page pins a bold, always-active “Buy Now” button. Tapping it before choosing a ticket just flashes a toast “Please select a ticket type” and does nothing.
Why it confusesThe CTA looks ready, but its precondition — pick a package — lives further up the page (the faint “SELECT A PACKAGE” hint is easy to miss). Users tap the obvious button, get bounced, then have to hunt for the selector.
Where in UICustomer app → Event detail → bottom action bar (“SELECT A PACKAGE” + “Buy Now”).
Suggested fixDisable / soften “Buy Now” until a package is chosen, or make tapping it scroll to and open the package selector instead of erroring.

Merchant dashboard — flow (from 08-22)

10 Reward Points shows a literal “undefined” in the redemption rate HIGH

ProblemThe Reward Points config card reads: “Earn 9 point per $1 spent; undefined points redeem $1.” — a raw JavaScript `undefined` printed where the redeem rate should be.
Why it confusesA merchant reading “undefined points redeem $1” has no idea what the redemption rate is, and it reads as an obvious bug — undermining trust in the whole points feature.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Promotions → Reward Points → Points Type (Cash Credits) description.
Suggested fixBind the redeem-rate value (currently undefined) and format the sentence; also “9 point” → “9 points”.

11 Dashboard KPIs mix time windows and don’t reconcile MED

ProblemThe Event Dashboard mixes “(Current Month)” metrics with all-time totals, and the attendance figures don’t add up: No-show (87) exceeds this month’s Registrations (85) and Total Check-ins (72); Avg Attendance 56.3% doesn’t follow from those numbers.
Why it confusesA merchant can’t tell which period a number covers, or how registrations / check-ins / no-shows relate. Figures that don’t reconcile make the whole dashboard feel untrustworthy.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Event Dashboard (Registration/Ticket Summary, Event Earnings, Attendance/Check-in).
Suggested fixLabel every metric’s period consistently (or separate all-time from current-month), and state the relationship (e.g. No-show = Registrations − Check-ins over the same scope) via tooltip.

12 Every order shows “Awaiting Confirmation” — even free $0 events MED

ProblemOn the Order List every order carries the status “Awaiting Confirmation”, including free ($0.00) event orders, which also show Ticket Count “-”.
Why it confusesA free event has nothing to confirm or pay, so the status is misleading; and because every order shows the same status, a merchant can’t triage what actually needs action.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Events → Order List (Status column).
Suggested fixAuto-confirm free orders, and give paid orders real states (Awaiting Payment / Paid / Completed / Refunded) so the column is actionable.

13 “Ongoing Events” lists past, today, and future — all “Published” MED

Problem“Ongoing Events” shows events dated in the past, today, and weeks out, every one tagged only “Published”. Nothing indicates which events are over.
Why it confuses“Ongoing” implies currently-active, but the list mixes finished and upcoming; “Published” is about visibility, not lifecycle.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Events → Ongoing Events (list).
Suggested fixIntroduce a lifecycle state (Upcoming / Live / Ended) distinct from “Published”, and scope “Ongoing” accordingly.

14 “Event Planning” and “Ongoing Events” are near-duplicate lists LOW

ProblemTwo sub-tabs — “Ongoing Events” and “Event Planning” — show effectively the same events with the same “Published” status, differing mainly in columns.
Why it confusesTwo near-identical event lists under one tab give a merchant no clear model of which to use for what.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Events → “Ongoing Events” vs “Event Planning”.
Suggested fixMerge into one events list, or make each sub-tab’s distinct purpose obvious rather than repeating the list.

15 Zelle/Venmo option is labeled for “marketplace / service booking” on an event merchant LOW

ProblemIn Payment Settings the Zelle/Venmo toggle reads “Collect payment via Zelle or Venmo for Marketplace Pick-up Orders or Service Booking” — but this is an event-only merchant.
Why it confusesA merchant can’t tell whether enabling it affects their event orders, since the description names contexts that don’t exist for them.
Where in UIMerchant dashboard → Financials → Payment Settings.
Suggested fixMake the helper text reflect the merchant’s enabled business type(s), or state plainly which order types Zelle/Venmo covers.
